newsitem.title: USA: Midday COMEX copper off on fund sales but rebounds.
newsitem.headline: Midday COMEX copper off on fund sales but rebounds.

text.p: COMEX copper fell at midday on ignited fund sell-stop orders below 107.00 cents a lb for September delivery, but rebounded slightly on arbitrage buying, floor sources said.
COMEX opened lower on another jump in LME warehouse stocks, which are currently at a 10-month high of 234,950 tonnes, nearly doubling in the last six weeks.
At 1223 EDT, Active September copper was down 1.50 cents at 107.40 cents a lb, with the spot month down the same at 107.30 cents.
"We opened 1.30 cents lower following London," a floor trader said. "We hit some fund stops below 107.00 and from then on in it was arbitrage buying."

Floor traders shrugged off news that 1,400 Canadian workers walked off the job at Falconbridge Ltd's Sudbury mine in Ontario, which produced 50,000 tonnes of copper last year. The union contract expired at midnight Friday.

In other news, Asarco Inc's chief executive officer reported his usual bullish copper projections at the company's quarterly analyst meeting, calling for a worldwide supply deficit of 34,000 short tons in 1997 and 173,000 short tons in 1998.
